**Park Ji-min** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"): 박지민[mononymously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mononym "Mononym") as **Jimin** , is a South Korean singer, songwriter, and dancer. In 2013, he made his debut as a member of the South Korean boy band [BTS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BTS "BTS"), under the record label [Big Hit Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Hit_Music "Big Hit Music"). Jimin has released three solo tracks under BTS' name—"Lie" in 2016, "[Serendipity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serendipity_\(BTS_song\) "Serendipity \(BTS song\)")" in 2017, and "Filter" in 2020—all of which have charted on South Korea's [Gaon Digital Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaon_Digital_Chart "Gaon Digital Chart").
He released his first credited solo song, the digital track "Promise", which he co-wrote, in 2018 and recorded the duet "[With You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/With_You_\(Jimin_song\) "With You \(Jimin song\)")" with [Ha Sung-woon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ha_Sung-woon "Ha Sung-woon") for the soundtrack for the [TvN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TvN_\(South_Korean_TV_channel\) "TvN \(South Korean TV channel\)") drama _[Our Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Blues "Our Blues")_ in 2022. Jimin released his debut solo album, _[Face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_\(Jimin_album\) "Face \(Jimin album\)")_ in 2023, which debuted at number one in South Korea and Japan and number two on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), making him the highest-charting Korean solo artist on the latter chart. The album's single "[Like Crazy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like_Crazy_\(song\) "Like Crazy \(song\)")" became the first song by a Korean solo artist to debut at number one on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") in history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-3) Jimin also became the first Korean solo artist to top the _Billboard_ [Artist 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist_100 "Artist 100") chart. In 2024, he released his second album, _[Muse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muse_\(Jimin_album\) "Muse \(Jimin album\)")_ , and its lead single "[Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who_\(song\) "Who \(song\)")", which debuted at number one on the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200").
## Early life and education
Park Ji-min was born on October 13, 1995, in [Geumjeong District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geumjeong_District "Geumjeong District"), [Busan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busan "Busan"), South Korea.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-4) He is of the [Milyang Park clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milyang_Park_clan "Milyang Park clan").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-5) His immediate family includes his mother, father, and younger brother.
When he was a child, he attended Busan's Hodong Elementary School and Yonsan Middle School.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-thestarprofile-2) In middle school, he attended Just Dance Academy, where he learned [popping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popping "Popping") and [locking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locking_\(dance\) "Locking \(dance\)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-6) Prior to becoming a trainee, Jimin studied [contemporary dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_dance "Contemporary dance") at Busan High School of Arts and was a top student in the [modern dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_dance "Modern dance") department.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-get_to_know-7) A teacher suggested that he join an entertainment company, leading him to [Big Hit Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Hit_Music "Big Hit Music"). Once he passed the auditions in 2012, he transferred to [Korean Arts High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_Arts_High_School "Korean Arts High School"), graduating in 2014.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-8)
Jimin graduated from [Global Cyber University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Cyber_University?action=edit&redlink=1 "Global Cyber University \(page does not exist\)") [[ko](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EA%B8%80%EB%A1%9C%EB%B2%8C%EC%82%AC%EC%9D%B4%EB%B2%84%EB%8C%80%ED%95%99%EA%B5%90 "ko:글로벌사이버대학교")] in August 2020 with a major in Broadcasting and Entertainment. He was awarded the President's Award, the school's highest honor.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-9) As of 2021, he is enrolled at [Hanyang Cyber University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanyang_Cyber_University "Hanyang Cyber University"), pursuing a [Master of Business Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Business_Administration "Master of Business Administration") in Advertising and Media.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-10)
## Career
### 2013–present: BTS
Main article: [BTS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BTS "BTS")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Park_Ji-min_performing_at_Incheon_Sky_Festival_in_September_2013_01.jpg/250px-Park_Ji-min_performing_at_Incheon_Sky_Festival_in_September_2013_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Park_Ji-min_performing_at_Incheon_Sky_Festival_in_September_2013_01.jpg)Jimin performing in September 2013
Jimin was the last Big Hit trainee to be added to the lineup that would eventually become [BTS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BTS "BTS"). Of the band's seven members, he spent the shortest period of time—six months—as a trainee prior to debuting.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-11) On June 13, 2013, he debuted as a [vocalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singing "Singing") and [dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance "Dance") in BTS with the song "No More Dream" from their first single _[2 Cool 4 Skool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2_Cool_4_Skool "2 Cool 4 Skool")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-12) Under the band's name, he released three solo songs: "Lie", "[Serendipity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serendipity_\(BTS_song\) "Serendipity \(BTS song\)")", and "Filter". "Lie" was released in 2016, as part of the band's second Korean studio album, _[Wings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wings_\(BTS_album\) "Wings \(BTS album\)")_. It was described as stunning and dramatic, conveying dark undertones and emotions in line with the overall concept of the album.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-13) In contrast, "[Serendipity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serendipity_\(BTS_song\) "Serendipity \(BTS song\)")", from the band's _[Love Yourself: Her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Yourself:_Her "Love Yourself: Her")_ (2017) [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") (EP), was soft and sensual, expressing the joy, conviction, and curiosity of love.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-14) "Filter", a track from BTS' 2020 studio album _[Map of the Soul: 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Map_of_the_Soul:_7 "Map of the Soul: 7")_ , had a [Latin pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_pop "Latin pop") flair, with lyrics reflecting the different sides of Jimin that he shows to the world and those around him.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-Filter_solo-15) Jimin additionally co-wrote and co-produced another track included on that album, "Friends", which was later featured in the [Marvel Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Studios "Marvel Studios") film _[Eternals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternals_\(film\) "Eternals \(film\)")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-16)
"Serendipity" and "Lie" both surpassed fifty million streams on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") in 2018, followed shortly thereafter by the former's full length version from BTS' _[Love Yourself: Answer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Yourself:_Answer "Love Yourself: Answer")_ (2018) compilation album, which achieved the milestone in early 2019. Jimin became the first Korean artist to have three solo tracks accumulate over 50 million streams each, surpassing [Psy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psy "Psy"), who previously crossed the 50 million streams mark twice with "[Gangnam Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangnam_Style "Gangnam Style")" (2012) and "[Gentleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentleman_\(Psy_song\) "Gentleman \(Psy song\)")" (2013).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-18) Both songs were also the only solos by a BTS member included in the [Official Charts Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company")'s (OCC) list of the top 20 most streamed BTS songs in the United Kingdom as of October 2018, ranking at number 17 and 19 respectively.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-19) In April 2019, the list was expanded to reflect the top 40, and both tracks were the highest ranked solos included that year, at numbers 18 and 20 respectively.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-officialcharts-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-21)
In May 2019, Jimin became the first BTS member to have a solo music video achieve 100 million views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") when "Serendipity" surpassed the milestone.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-23) He remained the only BTS member with multiple solo songs in the January 2020 update of the OCC's top 40 list: "Lie" and "Serendipity" were the second and third most-streamed solos, at numbers 24 and 29 respectively, with the full-length version of the latter at number 38.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-24)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-officialcharts-20) The following month, Jimin earned his first entry on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") with "Filter", which debuted at number 87 on the chart,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-25) as well his first number one on the World Digital Song Sales chart. The song set the record for the biggest streaming debut among all Korean songs on Spotify, accruing over 2.2 million streams in its first 24 hours of release, and went on to become the fastest Korean solo in the platform's history to surpass 20–60 million streams.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-27) It was also the only solo album track by BTS to receive a Song of the Year nomination at the [Gaon Chart Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaon_Chart_Music_Awards "Gaon Chart Music Awards").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-29) In March 2021, "Filter" became the 15th BTS song to spend a full year on _Billboard_ 's [World Digital Song Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Digital_Song_Sales "World Digital Song Sales") chart.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-31) It was the longest-charting Korean song released in 2020 on the ranking,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-32) having spent 80 weeks on the chart as of the issue dated October 9, 2021.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-33)
Jimin was awarded the fifth-class Hwagwan [Order of Cultural Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Cultural_Merit_\(South_Korea\) "Order of Cultural Merit \(South Korea\)") in 2018, alongside his bandmates, by the [President of South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_South_Korea "President of South Korea"), [Moon Jae-in](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon_Jae-in "Moon Jae-in"), for their contributions to the promotion of Korean culture.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-34) Three years later, Moon appointed him [Special Presidential Envoy for Future Generations and Culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_the_President_\(South_Korea\) "Office of the President \(South Korea\)"), alongside his bandmates, to help "lead the global agenda for future generations" and "expand South Korea's diplomatic efforts and global standing" in the international community.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-35)

## Artistry
[![Jimin stands on a stage holding his belt while dancing.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Jimin_on_Melon_Music_Awards_2016.jpg/250px-Jimin_on_Melon_Music_Awards_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jimin_on_Melon_Music_Awards_2016.jpg)Jimin performing "[Blood Sweat & Tears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_Sweat_&_Tears_\(BTS_song\) "Blood Sweat & Tears \(BTS song\)")" at the 2016 [Melon Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melon_Music_Awards "Melon Music Awards").
Jimin's vocals have been described as delicate and sweet.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-76) He is regarded as an exceptional dancer among the members of BTS and in K-pop in general,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-get_to_know-7)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-elite_daily-77) often praised for his "smooth and elegant movements" and charm on stage. In the documentary _[Burn the Stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burn_the_Stage:_The_Movie#Adaptation "Burn the Stage: The Movie")_ released in 2018, Jimin addressed his [perfectionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfectionism_\(psychology\) "Perfectionism \(psychology\)").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-elite_daily-77) In 2023, Jimin stated that as a pop artist, he "aims to excel at both dancing and singing and perform a diverse range of musical genres and themes" while "taking a healthy and sustainable approach to do so".[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-78)
He has cited singer [Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_\(entertainer\) "Rain \(entertainer\)") as an inspiration and one of the reasons why he wanted to become a singer and performer.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-79)
## Impact and influence
In 2016, Jimin was ranked as the 14th most popular idol in an annual survey conducted by [Gallup Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallup_Korea "Gallup Korea").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-80) He subsequently ranked seventh in 2017, and then consecutively ranked first in 2018 and 2019,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-81)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_] as the only idol to top the survey for two consecutive years.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-82) In 2018, Jimin was the ninth most-tweeted about celebrity and the eighth most-tweeted about musician globally.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-83) He was named the 17th best boy band member in history by _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-84) From January to May 2018, Jimin won the monthly "Top K-Pop Artist–Individual" award for _Peeper x Billboard_ , a collaboration between the _Peeper_ social media app and [_Billboard_ Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard \(magazine\)") that collects fan votes for their favorite K-pop artists. The prize was a donation to [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF") in his name.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-85)
The Cultural Conservation Society awarded Jimin a plaque of appreciation in 2019, for performing [buchaechum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchaechum "Buchaechum"), a traditional Korean fan dance, during the [2018 Melon Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Melon_Music_Awards "2018 Melon Music Awards") and helping spread the dance outside of Korea.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-86) In October 2021, he became the first idol to spend 34 consecutive months atop the brand reputation ranking for individual boy group idols[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-87) and the only one to top the overall ranking for three consecutive years.
Jimin is often cited as a role model by various idols in the [K-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-pop "K-pop") industry, many of whom try to emulate his style of dance, mannerisms, and stage presence; media outlets have called him the "Idol of Idols", "Idol's Bible", and "Rookies' Bible". Artists who have cited him as an influence include Arthur of [Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_\(group\) "Kingdom \(group\)"), Bic of [MCND](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCND "MCND"), Kim Si-hun of [BDC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BDC_\(group\) "BDC \(group\)"), Woochul of [Newkidd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newkidd "Newkidd"), [Hyunjin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyunjin_\(Stray_Kids_singer\) "Hyunjin \(Stray Kids singer\)") of [Stray Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stray_Kids "Stray Kids"), [Wooyoung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jung_Wooyoung "Jung Wooyoung") of [Ateez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ateez "Ateez"), Lim Se-jun of [Victon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victon "Victon"), [HueningKai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HueningKai "HueningKai") and [Beomgyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beomgyu "Beomgyu") of [Tomorrow X Together](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomorrow_X_Together "Tomorrow X Together"), and [Ni-Ki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ni-Ki "Ni-Ki") and Jay of [Enhypen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhypen "Enhypen").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-89) British internet personality [Oli London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oli_London "Oli London") underwent 15 cosmetic surgeries by 2020 to resemble Jimin.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-90)
Jimin has also been acknowledged beyond the [K-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-pop "K-pop") industry. In 2019, Award-winning director and photographer [Gus Van Sant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Van_Sant "Gus Van Sant") named him as the artist he wished to work with.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-91) In 2021, Olympic figure skater [Yuzuru Hanyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuzuru_Hanyu "Yuzuru Hanyu") shared being a [BTS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BTS "BTS") fan and mentioned Jimin as a source of inspiration for his dance movements on the rink.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-93) In 2023, [Ryan Gosling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Gosling "Ryan Gosling") gifted Jimin the guitar his character Ken used in the movie _[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_\(film\) "Barbie \(film\)")_ , as Jimin's "[Permission to Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permission_to_Dance "Permission to Dance")" music video outfit served as inspiration for one of the outfits Gosling wore for the role.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-95)

## Philanthropy
### Education
Jimin is a supporter of education and the arts. From 2016 to 2018, he covered uniform expenses of students at his alma mater, Busan Hodong Elementary School. After the school's closing was announced, he donated summer and winter middle school uniforms to the final graduates and gifted autographed albums to the entire student body.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-98) In early 2019, Jimin donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million (equivalent to ₩117.23 million or [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD")87,468.18 in 2025)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-inflation-KRW-99) to the Busan Department of Education to help support students from low income families. Of the total, [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")30 million (equivalent to ₩35.17 million or [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD")26,240.45 in 2025)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-inflation-KRW-99) went to his alma mater, Busan Arts High School.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-100) In July 2020, he donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million (equivalent to ₩116.61 million or [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD")87,000.74 in 2025)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-inflation-KRW-99) to the Jeonnam Future Education Foundation to fund the creation of a scholarship fund for talented students from [South Jeolla Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Jeolla_Province "South Jeolla Province") who were struggling financially.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-101)
In September 2022, Jimin made a donation to the Gangwon Provincial Office of Education.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-102) In March 2023, he donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")74,611.5) to the North Chungcheong Provincial Office of Education to fund books and reading education programs for students.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-103) In May 2024, he made a donation of [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")74,611.5) to the South Gyeongsang Provincial Office of Education to create a scholarship for underprivileged students.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-104) In September 2024, Jimin donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")74,611.5) to fund scholarships, along with living and medical expenses for Korean soldiers. The donation serves to support families of soldiers who have struggled, suffered a loss, or passed. Following his donation, Jimin was appointed to the honor society of the [Community Chest of Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_Chest_of_Korea "Community Chest of Korea")'s [Chungnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Chungcheong_Province "South Chungcheong Province") branch.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-105) In July 2025, he donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")74,611.5) to the Jeonbuk Office of Education in the North Jeolla Province. This marked his 6th donation since 2019 to Provincial Offices of Education for the creation of scholarships for deprived students.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-106)
### Other philanthropy
In July 2021, Jimin donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million (equivalent to ₩113.76 million or [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD")84,880.15 in 2025)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-inflation-KRW-99) to [Rotary International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotary_International "Rotary International") to help polio patients. As with previous donations, the benefaction was made privately but became public in September, when the Go-seong Rotary Club displayed a banner thanking him for the donation.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-107) He was announced as a member of the Green Noble Club, a group of major donors to the Green Umbrella Children's Foundation who have contributed ₩100 million or more, on October 12, 2021.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-108) In February 2023, he donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")74,611.5) through the Korean UNICEF Committee toward emergency relief for children affected by the [Turkey–Syria earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Turkey%E2%80%93Syria_earthquake "2023 Turkey–Syria earthquake").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-109)
In August 2023, Jimin participated in the "Hometown Love Donation System", a program allowing non-residents to donate to support welfare in [Nam District, Busan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_District,_Busan "Nam District, Busan"). He donated the maximum allowed donation amount of [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")5 million ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")3,730.57) and proceeded to re-donate his campaign's donor return gifts to people in need in the region.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-110) In February 2024, Jimin was inducted in the Nam-gu Hometown Love Donation System Donor Hall of Fame for his contribution to the district welfare programs.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-111)
In December 2024, Jimin donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")30 million ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")22,383.45) to the Busan Habitat Challenge, a project aiming to improve the living conditions of the elderly in the city.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-112) In March 2025, he donated [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")100 million ([US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")74,611.5) to support firefighters following the [wildfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_South_Korea_wildfires "2025 South Korea wildfires") in the [Gyeongbuk region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gyeongbuk "Gyeongbuk").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-113)
## Personal life
Since 2018, Jimin has lived in [Hannam-dong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannam-dong "Hannam-dong"), Seoul, South Korea, with his bandmates.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-115) In 2021, he purchased a property in the area worth [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")5.9 [billion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1,000,000,000 "1,000,000,000") (equivalent to ₩6.71 [billion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1,000,000,000 "1,000,000,000") or [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD")5.01 million in 2025)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-inflation-KRW-99).[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-116)
### Health
In 2017, during BTS' [Wings Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wings_Tour "The Wings Tour"), Jimin was unable to participate in the show in [Macau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macau "Macau") due to neck and shoulder cramping.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-117) The following year, while in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") for the [Love Yourself World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Yourself_World_Tour "Love Yourself World Tour"), he withdrew from the band's scheduled performance on _[The Graham Norton Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Graham_Norton_Show "The Graham Norton Show")_ because of "severe muscle pain in his neck and back", according to a statement released by [Big Hit Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Hit_Music "Big Hit Music").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-118)
In 2022, Jimin was hospitalized after having abdominal pain and a mild sore throat. He underwent [appendicitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendicitis "Appendicitis") surgery on January 31 and received a positive [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") diagnosis.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-119)
### Military service
On November 22, 2023, Big Hit announced through [Weverse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weverse "Weverse") that Jimin, along with bandmates [RM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RM_\(musician\) "RM \(musician\)"), [V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V_\(singer\) "V \(singer\)"), and [Jung Kook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jung_Kook "Jung Kook"), had started the enlistment process to carry out his [mandatory military service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_South_Korea "Conscription in South Korea").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-120) He enlisted as an active duty soldier on December 12 at the Army 5th Division Recruit Training Center in [Yeoncheon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeoncheon "Yeoncheon")[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-121) with Jung Kook using the buddy system.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-122) He completed his five weeks of basic training in January 2024, placing first as an outstanding trainee and received the Best trainee commendation award from the Division Commander, taking an oath as the representative of all trainees in his unit.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-124) He was then appointed to an Artillery Unit in the [5th Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5th_Infantry_Division_\(South_Korea\) "5th Infantry Division \(South Korea\)").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-125) In June, Jimin received an early promotion and was selected as a Special Class Warrior for his excellent military performance.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-126) He was formally discharged on June 11, 2025.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimin#cite_note-127)
